title: JiraSnapshotEntry
description: One `snapshot[jira_key]` entry — the single source of truth for the shape the reconciler's fetcher (PRODUCER) writes and the inbound/outbound differs (CONSUMERS) read. See docs/adr/0004-reconciler-snapshot-contract.md. It constrains the SHAPE of each contract key (types + nesting), never specific values, so it is not a change-detector. `additionalProperties` stays open: the entry is the raw `fields` map of a Jira issue merged with three enrichment keys, and Jira returns more fields than the reconciler reads. Load with `rebar.schemas.load('jira_snapshot_entry')`; validate with `rebar.schemas.validator('jira_snapshot_entry')`. The generated `JiraSnapshotEntry` TypedDict in `rebar/types.py` is derived from this file and is kept honest by the CI drift gate (`python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types --check`), so a fetcher field change must land here FIRST.

summary.description: Issue summary. Read by both differs (mapped to the local `title`).

description.description: ADF `doc` dict (REST v3) or plain text. Read by both differs, ADF-decoded.

status.description: `{"name": str, ...}` (or a bare name string). Read by both differs.

priority.description: `{"name": str, ...}` (or a bare name string / null). Read by both differs.

assignee.description: `{"displayName"/"accountId", ...}`, or null for an unassigned issue.

labels.description: Label strings. Read by the label differs (carries the `rebar-id:` binding label).

issuetype.description: `{"name": str, ...}` (or a bare name string). Read by both differs.

body.description: ADF `doc` dict (REST v3) or plain text.

comment.description: The NESTED comment field — bug 0ee6's seam. Comments live under `comment.comments`, NOT under a flat top-level `comments` key, which the top-level `not` clause forbids outright so a producer regressing to the flat shape fails validation. A horizon-trimmed issue carries the same shape with an EMPTY `comments` list.

issuelinks.description: REST-nested issue links (bug 3f04 carried none). An EMPTY list is the AUTHORITATIVE "queried, Jira reports no links" value; an ABSENT key means never queried.

parent.description: `{"key": str}`, or `null` for an issue that WAS queried and genuinely has no parent (the key is PRESENT with a falsy value). An ABSENT key means never queried — a truncated page walk, a cross-project issue, or `get_parent_map`'s `{}` degradation on any REST failure. Only the PRESENT-and-falsy form may authorise an inbound parent CLEAR, a write that DESTROYS local data (ticket 88d9; the history here contains a revert titled "Revert the inbound parent clear: it destroys data"). Do not collapse present-vs-absent. Per JSON Schema, `required` applies only when the value IS an object, so `null` validates.
